answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents stake tokens like roots beneath a willow or yarrow on a narrow ledge, establishing a verifiable credit graph. Game-theoretic multi-agent auditing conducts topological cut verifications across clusters; if an adversary creates fake identities to fake consensus, auditing agents slash their collateral. Because min-cut verification detects disjoint subgraphs, forcing attackers to fund every partition boundary, attacker cost scales superlinearly with network size.
